title: Hybrid hot/cold KV page allocator with epochal consolidation and continuous-batching alignment
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: Our KV cache fragmentation and tail-latency regressions remain the largest contributor to per-token cost variance on long-sequence workloads. Continuous batching reduces wasted device work but interacts poorly with existing variable-sized KV entries: fragmented allocations and frequent small frees create allocation churn and CUDA memory metadata blowups. Goal: implement an allocation strategy that reduces fragmentation, aligns GC/compaction with continuous-batching boundaries, and keeps per-request latency predictable while preserving high throughput.
proposed_solution: Introduce a hybrid hot/cold page allocator with the following components: 1) Fixed-size GPU 'pages' (e.g., 64KB) carved from larger pinned device buffers. Pages are tagged hot or cold based on access frequency and KV size histogram. 2) Hopscotch-style local remapping within a page group to pack variable-length KV entries without moving cold pages frequently. 3) Epochal consolidation worker: background compaction runs at batch-commit boundaries (aligned to continuous-batching flush points) to coalesce cold pages and reclaim fragmentation. 4) Batch-aware eviction policy: on eviction pressure, preferentially reclaim pages that are cold and align to upcoming batch windows to avoid mid-batch relocations. 5) Tenant-aware soft-reservations to reduce noisy-neighbor induced churn: reserve a small hot-page pool per tenant; overflow is spilled to a shared cold pool. 6) Lightweight per-page meta with 32-bit allocation bitmaps and a compact freelist; avoid per-KV allocation metadata on the CPU path to speed allocations. 7) Memory reclamation uses a two-phase retire/scan to ensure KV references in in-flight batches are not invalidated. Implementation notes: map pages into a small number of CUDA arenas to reduce fragmentation from CUDA allocator; use cudaMallocAsync where available; ensure stream-safety by deferring page frees until stream callbacks confirm no outstanding uses.
tradeoffs_and_risks:
- Complexity: introduces more allocator state and a background worker; risk of bugs causing stalls.
- Latency during consolidation: although aligned to batch boundaries, compaction can create transient spikes if not rate-limited.
- Memory overhead: page tagging and soft-reservations consume some headroom.
- Portability: cudaMallocAsync and pinned buffer strategies differ across drivers/hardware; need fallbacks.
- telemetry gaps: may need new signals to decide hot vs cold correctly for novel workloads.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement in feature branch behind 'hybrid-kv-allocator' FF. 2) Unit + fuzz tests for allocation/free semantics, stream-safety, and epoch retire paths. 3) Canary on internal infra with small tenant set and quota-limited traffic. 4) Add soft telemetry dashboards and synthetic benchmarks (long-context chat, streaming summarization). 5) Expand canary gradually: 5% -> 25% -> 100% of internal tenants. 6) Public rollout gated on sustained improvement in fragmentation ratio and no regression in p99 latency over 2 weeks.
telemetry_and_metrics: batch-aligned-relocations: number of KV moves executed at batch boundaries
p50/p95/p99 token latency for long-seq workloads
acceptance_criteria: Fragmentation ratio reduced by >=30% on our long-context synthetic workload (100k requests, 1M tokens each) compared to baseline
No more than 5% regression in p99 token latency across all production tenants during 2-week canary
Background compaction does not cause unexpected CUDA OOMs in canary fleet
Allocator passes fuzz tests including concurrent alloc/free and stream-fence scenarios
Telemetry for hot/cold classification validated against TTL-based oracle for at least two representative workloads
